correctness.rationale: The Plücker potential log det(I+Z*Z) gives metric h_Z(H,H)=tr(S^-1 H* T^-1 H), whose determinant equals det(S)^(-N). Thus the Ricci form equals 2N omega0 and g=2N g0 is Einstein with Ric(g)=g, matching the motivating paper's CP^p normalization at k=1. Chen--Deng--Zhang Lemmas 3.2 and 3.4 prove the intrinsic trace-metric geodesic distance as the Euclidean norm of principal angles and the maximum pi sqrt(k)/2 for N>=2k. Scaling yields diam squared=pi squared Nk/2; subtracting from pi squared m with m=k(N-k) gives pi squared k(N-2k)/2. The second Betti numbers 1 and k squared distinguish the balanced Grassmannian from the conjectured product equality model. The package checker reproduces exact matrix determinant and all normalization identities.

originality.rationale: The motivating full 2026 preprint states an equality-only-for-products conjecture and compares only projective spaces and their line-products. The second full primary paper proves the canonical intrinsic Grassmannian geodesic diameter but does not combine it with the Einstein normalization or identify counterexamples to the conjecture. The present derivation demonstrates an infinite family of irreducible non-product equality models by computing the normalized diameter and distinguishing cohomology. No published record checked in exact-claim, parameter, conjecture, or dual terminology states this contradiction. The distance and curvature components themselves are classical and are not presented as new individually.
residual_risks: The metric and Kähler–Einstein identities are classical, so an unindexed short observation may have previously combined them and noticed the same contradiction.
The classification of all possible equality cases under Ricci>=g is not addressed.
The universal diameter upper inequality may be true or false independently; the present family does not decide it.

value.rationale: The result gives a direct infinite family of irreducible homogeneous counterexamples to the equality-only-if-product part of a specific newly stated sharp Kähler diameter conjecture. It identifies the exact geometric reason: Einstein normalization of a higher-rank Grassmannian produces a diameter-to-dimension saturation precisely when the two plane dimensions balance. This excludes the stated rigidity classification and forces a substantive revision of any future equality theory, while leaving the conjectural upper inequality explicitly unresolved. This is a motivated counterexample to a natural extremal-geometry statement, not an arbitrary numerical case or relabeling.
